req.title: Redirect-to rejects invalid URL
req.statement: The system shall respond with HTTP 400 when the 'url' parameter of /redirect-to is missing or malformed.

doc.reasoning: The requirement states that /redirect-to must return HTTP 400 when the 'url' parameter is missing or malformed. Examining the source code (lines 572-644), the handler does `response.headers['Location'] = args['url'].encode('utf-8')` with no guard — if 'url' is absent, a KeyError is raised (which Flask converts to 500, not 400). This means the current implementation does NOT satisfy R-HTTPBIN-027 for the missing-url case. Tests must verify: (1) positive — valid url yields 3xx redirect with correct Location; (2) negative — missing url yields 400; (3) boundary — empty string url; (4) additional negative — malformed/non-URL string. Tests are written to be mutation-resilient by asserting exact status codes and exact header values.

tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app
client = app.test_client()

def test_redirect_to_valid_url_returns_302_with_location():
    r = client.get('/redirect-to?url=https://example.com', follow_redirects=False)
    assert r.status_code == 302
    assert r.headers['Location'] == 'https://example.com'
